title: Dhanteras 2026: Smart Gold & Silver Investments Today
description: Dhanteras is an auspicious occasion for many Indians to purchase gold and silver, symbolising prosperity and good fortune. Beyond traditional jewellery, moder.

faq.q: Is buying gold on Dhanteras purely symbolic?
faq.a: While deeply rooted in tradition and symbolism, buying gold on Dhanteras can also be a strategic financial decision. With various investment options available, it's an opportunity to grow your wealth alongside observing cultural practices.

faq.q: What are the tax implications of selling gold?
faq.a: The tax implications depend on the holding period and the type of gold product. Short-term capital gains (holding period up to 3 years) are taxed at your income slab rate. Long-term capital gains (holding period over 3 years) are taxed at 20% with indexation benefits, except for SGBs redeemed at maturity, which are tax-exempt.

faq.q: How are SGBs different from Gold ETFs?
faq.a: SGBs are government securities denominated in gold, offering a fixed interest rate and tax-exempt capital gains on maturity. Gold ETFs are mutual funds that invest in physical gold, traded on stock exchanges, offering market-linked returns without fixed interest.

faq.q: Can Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) buy Sovereign Gold Bonds?
faq.a: No, Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) are not eligible to purchase Sovereign Gold Bonds. Only resident individuals, HUFs, Trusts, Universities, and Charitable Institutions can invest in SGBs.

faq.q: What about making charges on gold jewellery?
faq.a: Making charges are the costs associated with designing and crafting gold jewellery, typically ranging from 8% to 25% of the gold's value. These charges are usually non-recoverable upon resale, making jewellery a less efficient investment compared to coins, bars, or digital gold.

faq.q: Is digital gold regulated by SEBI or RBI?
faq.a: No, digital gold is currently not regulated by SEBI or RBI. This means that investor protection and grievance redressal mechanisms might differ from regulated financial products like Gold ETFs or SGBs.
